- Both N–O bonds are removed/replaced by N–H bonds.
- The two aryl rings and all methoxy groups remain unchanged.

**Chemoselective reduction of an aromatic nitro group to an aniline.**

The encoded reaction is most consistent with **reduction of an aromatic nitro group to an aniline**:

\[
\mathrm{Ar{-}NO_2 \longrightarrow Ar{-}NH_2}
\]

The aromatic scaffold and methoxy substituents appear unchanged.

### Recommended reagent systems

**First choice — catalytic hydrogenation**
- **H₂, 5–10% Pd/C**
- Solvent: ethanol, methanol, ethyl acetate, or ethyl acetate/ethanol
- Usually room temperature under mild hydrogen pressure

This is likely the cleanest option if the molecule contains no other hydrogenation-sensitive groups.

### Useful alternatives

| Reagent system | Typical solvent/conditions | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| **Fe, NH₄Cl** | Ethanol/water, heating | Practical and generally chemoselective |
| **SnCl₂·2H₂O, HCl** | Ethanol or aqueous ethanol | Reliable; produces an amine salt and requires basification/workup |
| **Zn, NH₄Cl** | Alcohol/water | Mild metal-mediated alternative |
| **H₂, PtO₂** | Alcohol or ethyl acetate | Effective catalytic hydrogenation |
| **H₂, Raney Ni** | Alcohol | Effective, but may be less selective for other reducible groups |
| **Ammonium formate, Pd/C** | Methanol or ethanol | Transfer-hydrogenation alternative; avoids external H₂ |

### Practical recommendation

A reasonable initial condition would be:

> **H₂, 10% Pd/C, ethanol or ethyl acetate/ethanol, room temperature, until disappearance of the nitro starting material.**

If hydrogenation of another functional group is a concern, use:

> **Fe/NH₄Cl in aqueous ethanol**, or **Zn/NH₄Cl**.
